test: non-Markov test in single cells via sci-fate new/total RNA
log: LOOP 250 -- THE NON-MARKOV CLAIM, IN SINGLE CELLS
The obvious test -- does OLD RNA predict NEW RNA beyond TOTAL -- is algebraically
void: total = new + old exactly, so the two determine the third with no biology.
That is loop 231's confound in its purest form. This loop uses TIME instead, which
is not algebraically related to any count: if the process is Markov in S, two cells
in the same state transcribe the same way however long they have been in dex.

Z7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Destructive sampling stands: this asks whether history is visible ACROSS cells at
different treatment durations, not whether one cell's trajectory is non-Markov.
Time-since-treatment is a coarse summary of history -- a cell at 10 h that responded
late scores identically to one that responded early.
Cells are unsynchronised. Cell-cycle phase varies within every timepoint and is
itself a hidden state with its own history, so a pass has a cell-cycle reading as
well as a memory reading and Z4 does not separate them.
The labelling window defines 'now'; anything faster is invisible.
A FAIL bounds the memory term at this resolution rather than excluding it -- the
same limit loop 247 recorded, and single cells do not remove it.
